If you think the SOC is quiet this week because it’s nearly Christmas... I have some bad news. 🧵👇

1

Alireza Gharib's avatar

1/5 CISA just added 3 "Old School" style bugs to the KEV catalog. 🛠️ SonicWall SMA1000 (CVE-2025-40602): Authorization bypass. 💻 ASUS Live Update (CVE-2025-59374): Malicious code in the updater. This isn't high-tech AI hacking. This is "Back to Basics."

1

Alireza Gharib's avatar

2/5 The Big Trend: Russian state actors (Sandworm) are officially "getting lazy" because we’re making it too easy. Amazon reports they’re ditching zero-days for misconfigured routers and VPNs. Why pick a lock when the window is wide open?

1

Alireza Gharib's avatar

3/5 Why this hurts: The ASUS bug is a supply chain nightmare. We tell users "Update your drivers!" and then the driver update contains a backdoor. It erodes the fundamental trust we need to keep a network healthy.

1

Alireza Gharib's avatar

4/5 Analysis: We are suffering from "Visibility Overload" but "Context Poverty." We have all the logs, but we’re missing the fact that a "Service Account" is suddenly running packet captures on a VPN gateway. 🚩

1

Alireza Gharib's avatar

Follow

5/5 The Triage: ✅ Audit all SonicWall SMA1000 instances. ✅ Disable ASUS Live Update on high-value workstations until you've verified the patch. ✅ Check your "Edge" devices for unexpected local admin logins. Stay vigilant, Blue Team.🛡️☕#CyberSecurity#BlueTe
